"IMPOSTER — NEXT DEVELOPMENT UPDATE

I want to make a focused improvement to my existing Imposter party game.

IMPORTANT: Do not rebuild the game. Do not redesign everything. Preserve the existing working features, game logic, and cream-and-lime-green visual identity.

I want to develop slowly, one feature at a time.

FIRST: REMOVE THESE FEATURES FROM THE CURRENT ROADMAP

Do not implement these features yet:

- Hindi language support.
- Additional language support.
- Custom word packs.
- QR code word sharing.
- Player avatars.

Keep the current player setup and English word categories.

Do not spend development time on these postponed features.

FEATURE 1: PARTY MATCH HISTORY AND STATISTICS

Add a persistent party statistics system.

The game should allow users to create a party consisting of a group of named players.

Example:

Party name: My Friends

Players:

- Alex
- Jordan
- Taylor
- Miz
- Sam
- Chris

When this group plays multiple matches, automatically track their results.

Statistics to track

For every player, record:

1. Total matches played.
2. Total matches won.
3. Number of times selected as Imposter.
4. Number of wins as Imposter.
5. Number of times caught as Imposter.
6. Number of normal-player wins.

Leaderboards

Create a party statistics screen containing:

- Most matches won.
- Most frequent Imposter.
- Most successful Imposter.
- Most frequently caught Imposter.
- Overall player leaderboard.

Show player names, statistics, and rankings in a clean interface.

Persistence

Statistics must remain saved when:

- A new round starts.
- The application is closed.
- The application is reopened.

Use reliable local storage appropriate to the existing application architecture.

Party management

Allow users to:

- Create a new party.
- Reuse an existing party.
- View party match history.
- View individual player statistics.
- Reset party statistics after confirmation.
- Start a fresh party without mixing its statistics with another party.

Keep the system simple.

Do not introduce online accounts or cloud multiplayer.

Important scoring rules

- Award points only after a completed match.
- Do not award points twice for the same match.
- Correctly handle multiple Imposters.
- Attribute wins to the correct winning team.
- Do not count incomplete or abandoned rounds as completed matches.

FEATURE 2: IMPOSTER WORD HINT SETTING

Add a toggle to the game setup screen.

Setting label:

\"Give Imposters word hints?\"

Description:

\"Give Imposters a small hint about the secret word to make the game easier for them.\"

When OFF:

- Imposters receive no hints.
- Existing gameplay remains unchanged.

When ON:

- Each Imposter receives a private, carefully generated hint.
- Hints must be relevant to the secret word.
- Hints must not reveal the actual secret word.
- Hints should be vague enough to preserve the challenge.
- All Imposters should receive the same hint unless the game mode requires otherwise.

Example:

Secret word: Strawberry.

Imposter hint: \"It's a fruit.\"

The normal players should continue seeing the actual secret word.

The Imposter should see only their assigned hint, never the actual word.

Show this hint privately during the role reveal.

Make sure this setting works with multiple Imposters.

FEATURE 3: OPTIONAL TYPED CLUE ROUND

The existing game has a clue-entry screen.

It displays:
\"One clue. Keep it clever.\"

It asks each player to enter a one-word clue before voting.

I want this feature to become optional.

Add a setup toggle:

\"Enable typed clue round?\"

Description:

\"Players enter a clue on their turn before voting.\"

When ON:

- Preserve the current clue-entry screen.
- Each player submits one clue.
- Display submitted clues.
- Continue to discussion and voting as usual.

When OFF:

- Skip the entire typed clue-entry phase.
- Do not display the clue input.
- Do not require clue submissions.
- Proceed directly to the discussion phase and then voting.
- Preserve the existing voting system.
- Preserve all existing winning conditions.

IMPORTANT:

Disabling typed clues must never disable voting.

Do not remove the existing clue feature. Make it optional.

FEATURE 4: SETUP SCREEN DESIGN

Place both new gameplay settings on the existing setup screen:

1. Give Imposters word hints?
2. Enable typed clue round?

Use attractive, compact toggle controls matching the existing design.

Requirements:

- Clearly display ON and OFF states.
- Explain each setting briefly.
- Save the settings locally.
- Preserve the selected settings when starting another round.
- Allow users to change them before starting a new game.

Do not overcrowd the setup screen.

DEVELOPMENT APPROACH

Before changing anything:

1. Inspect the current project.
2. Understand the existing player management.
3. Understand how match results are calculated.
4. Understand the current clue phase.
5. Understand how secret roles and words are distributed.
6. Identify the existing persistence mechanism.

Then implement these features without breaking the existing functionality.

Implement in this order:

PHASE 1: Both setup toggles and their actual gameplay behavior.

PHASE 2: Persistent party statistics and match history.

PHASE 3: Test everything.

Do not create visual-only controls.

Every toggle must actually change the gameplay.

Every statistic must come from real completed matches.

Test both ON and OFF states.

Test multiple Imposters.

Test restarting the application.

Test that the statistics do not get mixed between different parties.

Do not add the postponed features.

FINAL GOAL:

Make the existing Imposter game more customizable and replayable while keeping it simple, polished, reliable, and easy to play with friends using one shared phone.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing Imposter party game without rebuilding it, adding optional Imposter hints and typed clues, plus persistent party statistics and match history.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing game logic, features, cream-and-lime-green identity, player setup, English categories, and voting/win conditions.
- Do not implement Hindi or other languages, custom word packs, QR word sharing, or player avatars.
- Implement in order: toggles and gameplay behavior; party statistics/history; testing.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing Imposter party game with optional Imposter hints and typed clues, plus locally persistent party statistics and match history, without rebuilding it.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing game flow, cream-and-lime-green identity, player setup, English categories, and voting/win conditions.
- Settings persist locally; hints must not reveal the secret word to Imposters.
- Count completed matches once, with correct team attribution for multiple Imposters.
- Support named parties, party reuse, isolated party data, party and individual stats, match history, and confirmed resets.
- Do not implement other languages, custom word packs, QR word sharing, or player avatars.

## Decisions
- Use existing `localStorage` persistence and `finishGame()` as the match scoring point.
- Store each party’s players, scores, stats, and history separately; keep settings shared locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added partial party initialization, switching/creation UI, persistent hint and clue toggles, and a party stats view.
- Added hint display for Imposters and a clue-round bypass that proceeds to discussion or voting.
- Added completed-match score/stat/history recording with a duplicate-match guard and confirmed party reset.
- Removed the custom word pack control and removed custom pack state/use from category selection.

### Active
- Finish the feature implementation and resolve any integration issues.
- Test both toggle states, multiple Imposters, party isolation, match scoring/history, reset confirmation, and persistence across reloads.

### Blocked
- No external blocker; changes remain uncommitted and have not been tested.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `app.js` for stale custom-pack references and verify the current implementation parses and runs.
2. Review stats/history rendering, party isolation, and scoring for correctness.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests covering the required gameplay and persistence cases.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, settings, party persistence, hints/clues, scoring, and stats/history rendering.
- `styles.css`: Existing visual styles; may need styles for newly added party and stats UI.
- `index.html`: App shell and script/style loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` has uncommitted edits. A `renderStats()` implementation was recently added, but no validation followed.
- Check for references to removed `state.customPacks` and `openPackModal`; the custom pack function may still remain.
- `finishGame()` uses `state.completedMatchId` as an in-memory duplicate guard and records match history in the active party.
- Party switching reuses stored party records; party creation currently seeds the new party with the current player list.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Imposter party game’s optional hints and typed clues, plus locally persistent party statistics and match history, without rebuilding it.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game flow, cream-and-lime-green identity, player setup, English categories, and voting/win conditions.
- Persist settings locally; hints must not reveal the secret word to Imposters.
- Count completed matches once and correctly attribute team wins with multiple Imposters.
- Support named, reusable parties with isolated players, scores, stats, and history; show party and individual stats; confirm resets.
- Do not add other languages, custom word packs, QR word sharing, or player avatars.

## Decisions
- Use `localStorage` and `finishGame()` as the match scoring point.
- Store party data separately per party; keep settings shared locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added party creation/switching, persistent hint and clue toggles, Imposer hints, typed clue flow, scoring/history, stats view, and confirmed party reset.
- Removed the custom word pack control and custom pack use from category selection.
- `node --check app.js` passed before the latest edit.

### Active
- Fix and complete the feature implementation; verify UI styling, party isolation, stats/history, and gameplay behavior.
- Validate changes after the most recent edit to `app.js`.

### Blocked
- The latest `app.js` edit may have introduced a syntax issue: an extra blank-space line was inserted after the `settings` property in `state`; validation has not been rerun.
- Browser tests have not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and correct the latest edit in `app.js`; remove the stale `openPackModal()` function and any stale custom-pack references.
2. Review and test clue flow when disabled, hints on/off, multiple-Imposter scoring, party isolation, match history, reset confirmation, and persistence across reloads.
3. Check stats/history UI styling in `styles.css`, then run syntax and browser tests.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, settings, party persistence, hints/clues, scoring, and stats/history rendering.
- `styles.css`: Existing styles; check whether newly added party and stats UI needs styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` has uncommitted changes.
- `finishGame()` uses `state.completedMatchId` as an in-memory duplicate guard and records match history in the active party.
- Party creation seeds a new party with the current player list.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Imposter party game’s optional hints and typed clues, plus locally persistent party statistics and match history, without rebuilding it.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game flow, cream-and-lime-green identity, player setup, English categories, and voting/win conditions.
- Persist settings locally; hints must not reveal the secret word to Imposters.
- Count completed matches once and correctly attribute team wins with multiple Imposters.
- Support named, reusable parties with isolated players, scores, stats, and history; show party and individual stats; confirm resets.
- Do not add other languages, custom word packs, QR word sharing, or player avatars.

## Decisions
- Use `localStorage` and `finishGame()` as the match scoring point.
- Store party data separately per party; keep settings shared locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added party creation/switching, locally persistent hint and clue toggles, Imposter hints, typed clue flow, scoring/history, stats view, and confirmed party reset.
- Removed custom word pack controls/use and deleted the stale `openPackModal()` function.
- New parties now initialize without copying the current party’s players.
- Added responsive party and stats/history styles.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass; Chromium headless loaded `index.html` and rendered the setup screen.

### Active
- Verify party isolation and persistence, clue/hint toggles, multiple-Imposter scoring, stats/history, and reset confirmation through gameplay/browser testing.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction tests have not been performed; available Chromium check only dumped the initial setup DOM.

## Next Move
1. Run browser interaction tests for gameplay, party switching/isolation, scoring, stats/history, reset, and persistence across reloads.
2. Fix any issues revealed by those tests.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, settings, party persistence, hints/clues, scoring, and stats/history rendering.
- `styles.css`: Existing styles plus new party and stats/history styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Imposter party game’s optional hints and typed clues, plus locally persistent party statistics and match history, without rebuilding it.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game flow, cream-and-lime-green identity, player setup, English categories, and voting/win conditions.
- Persist settings locally; hints must not reveal the secret word to Imposters.
- Count completed matches once and correctly attribute team wins with multiple Imposters.
- Support named, reusable parties with isolated players, scores, stats, and history; show party and individual stats; confirm resets.
- Do not add other languages, custom word packs, QR word sharing, or player avatars.

## Decisions
- Use `localStorage` and `finishGame()` as the match scoring point.
- Store party data separately per party; keep settings shared locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added party creation/switching, locally persistent hint and clue toggles, Imposter hints, typed clue flow, scoring/history, stats view, and confirmed party reset.
- Removed custom word pack controls/use and stale `openPackModal()`.
- New parties initialize without copying current party players.
- Added responsive party and stats/history styles.

- Browser interaction verified initial setup and party creation/isolation, then attempted gameplay testing.

### Active
- Complete browser tests for clue/hint toggles, multiple-Imposter scoring, stats/history, reset confirmation, and persistence across reloads.
- Investigate the failed multiple-Imposter win assertion and distinguish a flawed test voting strategy from a game issue.

### Blocked
- Full gameplay test did not complete: it failed at `ASSERT: all multiple imposters caught for team win`; the test’s chosen votes may not satisfy the existing win condition.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the voting resolution and generate a valid vote pattern that exercises the multiple-Imposter team-win case.
2. Rerun browser interaction tests through scoring, party stats/history, reset, and reload persistence; fix any issues revealed.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, settings, party persistence, hints/clues, scoring, and stats/history rendering.
- `styles.css`: Party and stats/history styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Browser testing uses Chromium remote debugging on port `9222` and the app at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/index.html`.
- `resolveVotes()` only declares the room win when the top-vote leaders are exactly all Imposters: `caught.length===imposters.length&&leaders.length===imposters.length`.

NEXT UPDATE — IMPROVE NO-TYPED-CLUE GAMEPLAY AND SECRET WORD REVEAL

I want to make two specific improvements to my existing IMPOSTER party game.

IMPORTANT:
Do not rebuild the application.
Do not change unrelated features.
Do not redesign the entire interface.
Preserve all existing working functionality, styling, game settings, voting logic, statistics, and scoring.

Only implement the changes described below.

FEATURE 1: IMPROVE GAME FLOW WHEN TYPED CLUE ROUND IS OFF

The game already has a setting called:

"Enable typed clue round?"

When ON, everything currently works correctly.

DO NOT CHANGE THE ON behavior.

I want to improve what happens when this setting is OFF.

CURRENT PROBLEM

After all players have revealed their secret roles, the game should not require anyone to type clues.

Everyone is physically together and can communicate verbally.

Therefore, the typed clue-entry screen must be completely skipped.

REQUIRED NEW GAME FLOW

STEP 1 — ROLE REVEAL

Every player receives their private role using the existing pass-the-phone system.

Normal players see their secret word.

Imposters see their assigned role and any enabled hint.

STEP 2 — LAST PLAYER FINISHES ROLE REVEAL

When the last player presses the final continue button, check the typed clue setting.

If typed clue round is OFF, navigate to a NEW STARTING PLAYER SCREEN.

Do not navigate to the typed clue-entry screen.

STEP 3 — RANDOM STARTING PLAYER

Randomly select ONE player from the current party.

Display an attractive screen showing:

Small heading:
"ROUND 1 · GAME START"

Main heading:
"Who's starting?"

Display the randomly selected player's name prominently.

Example:

"Jordan"

Supporting text:

"You're the first to give a clue!"

Add an instruction:

"Start the discussion by saying your clue out loud. No typing required."

The randomly selected starting player can be any eligible player, including an Imposter.

Do not always select the first player in the player list.

Randomize the selection for every new round.

STEP 4 — START GAME SCREEN

Add a prominent button:

"START THE GAME"

When pressed, show or confirm that the verbal discussion phase has begun.

The group can now discuss the secret word and give clues verbally.

There must be NO text input.

There must be NO clue submission requirement.

STEP 5 — CONTINUE TO VOTING

At the bottom of the starting-player screen, provide a clear button:

"CONTINUE TO VOTING →"

When pressed, navigate directly to the EXISTING voting screen.

Reuse the existing voting functionality without changing its logic.

The voting screen must continue working exactly as before.

IMPORTANT GAME FLOW RULES

When typed clue round is OFF:

Role Reveal → Random Starting Player → Verbal Discussion → Existing Voting → Existing Results.

When typed clue round is ON:

Role Reveal → Existing Typed Clue Round → Existing Discussion/Voting Flow → Existing Results.

Do not mix these two flows.

Do not accidentally disable voting when typed clues are OFF.

Do not generate duplicate starting-player selections during a single round.

Store the selected starting player for the current round so refreshing or navigating backward does not unexpectedly change the selection.

For the next round, randomly select a new starting player.

FEATURE 2: DISPLAY CATEGORY DURING NORMAL PLAYER ROLE REVEAL

Improve the existing private role reveal screen.

Currently, normal players see their secret word.

I want the word category displayed underneath it.

NORMAL PLAYER EXAMPLE

Secret word:

CAT

Category:

ANIMAL

Design:

- Display the secret word prominently.
- Display CATEGORY as a small uppercase label underneath.
- Display the actual category directly below it.
- Use the existing cream and lime-green visual style.
- Maintain the current typography and spacing.

IMPOSTER SCREEN

Do not reveal the secret word.

Do not reveal the secret word's category.

The Imposter should only see:

"YOU ARE THE IMPOSTER"

If the optional Imposter word hint setting is enabled, show the assigned hint according to its existing behavior.

Do not accidentally expose the category through the Imposter hint or any shared screen.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Get the category from the same word data object used to select the secret word.
- Do not hardcode categories.
- Ensure every word has a valid category.
- If a category is missing, handle it gracefully.
- Keep secret information private to the current player's reveal screen.
- Do not expose the secret word or category on shared screens before the reveal phase is over.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS

Test all of these scenarios:

1. Typed clues ON: Existing gameplay must remain unchanged.
2. Typed clues OFF: Role reveal must lead to the new starting-player screen.
3. The selected starting player must be randomized.
4. Imposters must also be eligible to start.
5. The START THE GAME button must work.
6. CONTINUE TO VOTING must open the existing voting screen.
7. Voting and results must work normally.
8. A new round should select a new starting player.
9. Normal players must see both the secret word and its category.
10. Imposters must never see the secret word or category.
11. The optional Imposter hint must continue working.
12. Existing party statistics and scoring must remain correct.

Before implementation, inspect the current project and reuse its existing state management and navigation.

Do not create fake buttons or visual-only screens.

Implement actual working functionality.

FINAL REQUIREMENT:

Keep the game simple, smooth, private, and enjoyable for people playing together using one shared phone.

- Use the existing `state.phase` navigation and `state.roles`/word selection.

## Objective
- Complete optional typed/verbal clues and locally persistent party statistics/history in the existing Imposter game.
- When typed clues are off, show a randomized starting player and proceed through verbal discussion into voting.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing game flow, styling, settings, voting/win conditions, statistics, scoring, parties, and persistence; avoid unrelated changes or a rebuild.
- Keep typed clues ON unchanged; when OFF, use verbal clues and proceed directly to voting.
- Keep the starting player consistent for a round and select a new one next round; any player, including an Imposter, may start.
- Show normal players the secret word and its data-derived category; never show Imposters the word or category. Keep optional Imposter hints working.
- Test both gameplay paths, starting-player behavior, voting/results, privacy, hints, and statistics/scoring.

## Decisions
- Use the existing `state.phase` navigation and `state.roles`/word selection.
- Use the selected word’s category from `WORDS`; use a generic hint to avoid exposing the category to Imposters.
- Store the starting-player choice in `localStorage` under `imposter.startingPlayer`, keyed by match and party.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `wordCategory`, `startingPlayer`, and `verbalStarted` state fields and phase dispatch for `startingPlayer` and `verbalDiscussion`.
- Normal-player role reveal shows the secret word and category; Imposter reveal omits both and retains the optional generic hint.
- Final role-reveal navigation preserves the typed-clue path and routes typed-clues-off games to `startingPlayer`.
- Added starting-player and verbal-discussion screens, including direct continuation to voting and timer behavior.
- Added category and verbal-flow styles in `styles.css`.
- Ran browser test covering privacy, hints, categories, verbal timer/voting, typed clues/voting, results, history, and scores; it passed before adding the next-round rotation assertion.

### Active
- Validate that each consecutive round selects a different starting player; update the temporary test assertion to compare against the immediately preceding round.
- Re-run browser test, `node --check app.js`, and `git diff --check`.
- Review final diff and confirm typed-clue flow remains unchanged.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix the browser test’s rotation assertion to compare consecutive rounds, then rerun it in Chromium.
2. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
3. Review the final diff and report any testing limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, role reveals, phase routing, starting-player selection, voting, scoring, and stats.
- `styles.css`: Existing visual system and new category/verbal-flow styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/imposter-test.html`: Temporary browser test harness for gameplay paths and next-round starting-player rotation.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- `startGame()` creates a new `matchId`; game state and match ID are not restored on refresh.
- `getStartingPlayer()` now avoids the previous starter for the same party when selecting for a new match; test that the starter changes between consecutive rounds, not across non-consecutive rounds.

UI REPAIR — FIX BROKEN LAYOUT, STYLING AND THEME

The latest changes have broken the application's visual layout and overall theme.


I want you to thoroughly inspect and repair the entire UI.


IMPORTANT: This is a UI restoration and polishing task, NOT a game rebuild.


1. RESTORE THE ORIGINAL DESIGN


Restore the original visual identity of the IMPOSTER game.


The original design used:


- Warm cream/off-white background.
- Lime-green accent colors.
- Dark forest-green text and buttons.
- Clean white cards with subtle borders.
- Rounded corners.
- Elegant, modern typography.
- Generous spacing and consistent alignment.
- Minimal, polished party-game aesthetics.


The application should look cohesive and professionally designed.


Do not randomly introduce new colors, gradients, fonts, or visual styles.


2. FIX THE BROKEN LAYOUT


Inspect EVERY screen and repair:


- Incorrect component positioning.
- Broken card dimensions.
- Overlapping elements.
- Inconsistent margins and padding.
- Buttons extending outside their containers.
- Text overflowing or getting cut off.
- Misaligned headings and labels.
- Incorrect screen heights.
- Unnecessary empty spaces.
- Broken scrolling.
- Elements that become inaccessible on smaller screens.


Make sure the interface works properly on:


- Small Android phones.
- Large Android phones.
- Tablets.
- Desktop browsers.


Use responsive layouts rather than fixed dimensions that break on different screens.


3. RESTORE VISUAL CONSISTENCY


Every screen must follow the same design system.


Pay particular attention to:


- Home/setup screen.
- Player management.
- Game settings.
- Private role reveal.
- Starting player screen.
- Typed clue screen.
- Voting screen.
- Results screen.
- Match history.
- Statistics and scoreboard.


Cards, buttons, inputs, headings, labels, and spacing should look consistent throughout the application.


4. BUTTONS AND INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS


Repair the appearance and positioning of all interactive elements.


Ensure:


- Buttons have consistent heights and padding.
- Text is properly centered.
- Selected options are visually distinguishable.
- Toggles clearly show ON/OFF states.
- Inputs have proper borders and focus states.
- Disabled buttons look disabled.
- Touch targets are comfortable on mobile.


Do not leave any decorative or non-functional controls pretending to be interactive.


5. PRESERVE ALL GAME FUNCTIONALITY


This is extremely important.


Do not break or remove any existing features.


Preserve:


- Player creation and removal.
- Random player selection.
- Imposter assignment.
- Multiple Imposter settings.
- Secret word generation.
- Word categories.
- Imposter hints.
- Typed clue ON/OFF setting.
- Verbal discussion mode.
- Starting player selection.
- Voting.
- Final word guessing.
- Results.
- Match history.
- Player statistics.
- Scoring.
- Next-round functionality.


Do not rewrite the game logic unless absolutely necessary to fix a UI-related integration problem.


6. TECHNICAL INSPECTION


Before making changes:


1. Inspect the existing project structure.
2. Identify the components and styles responsible for the broken layout.
3. Check for conflicting CSS rules and duplicated styling.
4. Check whether recent changes introduced incorrect responsive behavior.
5. Identify any broken component nesting or layout constraints.
6. Fix the actual underlying causes instead of adding random CSS overrides.


Use reusable styling and consistent design tokens wherever possible.


7. FINAL QUALITY CHECK


After fixing everything:


- Open and inspect every screen.
- Test the full game flow.
- Check mobile responsiveness.
- Verify that no elements overlap.
- Verify that no text is clipped.
- Verify that scrolling works.
- Verify that the original theme is consistent.
- Verify that all buttons and settings still work.


Do not stop after fixing just the home screen.


The entire application must be visually consistent and functional.


FINAL GOAL:


Make IMPOSTER look like a professionally finished mobile party game, with its original cream, dark-green and lime-green identity fully restored.


Prioritize fixing the existing layout and theme before adding any new features.

## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game’s UI while preserving its original cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep all gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence functionality intact.

## Requirements
- Thoroughly inspect and repair layouts and styling across all screens, including mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use consistent responsive design, spacing, typography, cards, buttons, inputs, and interactive states.
- Preserve player management, Imposter assignment, words/categories, hints, typed and verbal clues, starting-player selection, voting, guessing, results, history, statistics, scoring, and next-round functionality.
- Avoid rebuilding the game, removing features, or making unrelated logic changes.
- Verify the full game flow, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat this as a UI restoration and polishing task, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve the existing `state.phase` flow, role and word selection, and previously added verbal clue behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Previously added verbal clue flow, category-aware role reveals, rotating starting-player selection, and local party history/statistics.
- Previously tested privacy, hints, categories, starting-player behavior, verbal and typed clue paths, results, history, and scores.
- Inspected `index.html`, `styles.css`, and the beginning of `app.js`; confirmed `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.

### Active
- Diagnose and repair the full application UI and styling; the requested UI work has not yet been implemented or verified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete stylesheet, app screen templates, and repository structure; identify the source of the broken visual layout and any conflicting or duplicated CSS.
2. Implement focused, reusable responsive styling that restores the existing design system across every screen without changing game logic unnecessarily.
3. Run the full gameplay and responsive UI checks, and report any coverage limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Current styling; includes recently added verbal-flow styles and is the primary UI repair target.
- `app.js`: Screen rendering, game flow, and statistics; inspect templates and preserve behavior.
- `index.html`: App shell, font imports, and theme metadata.

## Important Context
- Current uncommitted changes are in `app.js` and `styles.css`.
- `git diff --check` passed during the recent inspection; the recorded diff was 60 changed lines in `app.js` and 19 in `styles.css`.

- Repair layouts and styling across all screens for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use consistent responsive spacing, typography, cards, buttons, inputs, and interactive states.
- Preserve existing game features and flow; avoid rebuilding the game or making unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game UI while preserving its cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence intact.

## Requirements
- Repair layouts and styling across all screens for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use consistent responsive spacing, typography, cards, buttons, inputs, and interactive states.
- Preserve the existing game features and flow; avoid rebuilding the game or making unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat this as UI restoration and polishing, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve the existing `state.phase` flow, role and word selection, and verbal clue behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Previously added verbal clue flow, category-aware role reveals, rotating starting-player selection, and local party history/statistics.
- Previously tested privacy, hints, categories, starting-player behavior, verbal and typed clue paths, results, history, and scores.

### Active
- Diagnose and repair the full application UI and styling; requested UI work has not yet been implemented or verified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete stylesheet and all app screen templates; identify broken layout causes and conflicting or missing CSS.
2. Implement focused, reusable responsive styling without unnecessary game-logic changes.
3. Run gameplay and responsive UI checks; report any coverage limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Primary UI repair target; current content appears to contain only verbal-flow styles, while `HEAD` has the original single-line stylesheet.
- `app.js`: Screen rendering, game flow, and statistics; preserve existing behavior.
- `index.html`: App shell, font imports, and theme metadata.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Latest inspection found `git diff --check` passed; `app.js` has 60 changed lines and `styles.css` has 19 changed lines.
- `styles.css` appears to have replaced the original stylesheet with verbal-clue styles, likely breaking layouts across the app.

## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game UI while preserving its cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence intact.

## Requirements
- Repair layouts and styling across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use consistent responsive spacing, typography, cards, buttons, inputs, and interactive states.
- Preserve game flow and avoid unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat the work as UI restoration and polishing, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve `state.phase`, role and word selection, and verbal clue behavior.
- Restore the original stylesheet, then append focused responsive and accessibility refinements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Restored the original stylesheet rules that had been lost from `styles.css`.
- Added responsive party-bar and statistics/history layouts, verbal-flow styling, focus-visible outlines, disabled-button states, and reduced-motion handling.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Chromium headless smoke checks rendered the desktop setup and captured a mobile screenshot.

### Active
- Finish visual and interaction verification across gameplay screens and responsive sizes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the mobile screenshot and check computed layout for overflow/clipping at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
2. Exercise setup, role reveal, verbal discussion, voting, results, stats, and history in-browser; fix any issues found.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Restored base styling plus new responsive refinements.
- `app.js`: Existing screen templates, game flow, statistics, and persistence; preserve behavior.
- `index.html`: App shell and stylesheet/font loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- `styles.css` changed from a verbal-clue-only stylesheet to the original base stylesheet plus 105 lines of responsive and interaction styling.
- Desktop smoke output contained `.hero-line`, `.party-bar`, and `.setup-grid`; mobile capture saved to `/tmp/opencode/imposter-mobile.png`.

import json, os, socket, struct, subprocess, time, urllib.request
PORT=9237
proc=subprocess.Popen(['chromium','--headless=new','--no-sandbox','--disable-gpu','--remote-debugging-port='+str(PORT),'--user-data-dir=/tmp/opencode/cdp-audit-profile','about:blank'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
try:
    for _ in range(100):
        try:
            pages=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/json/list'))
            page=next(x for x in pages if x['type']=='page')
            break
        except Exception: time.sleep(.1)
    u=page['webSocketDebuggerUrl'].replace('localhost','127.0.0.1')
    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    p=urlparse(u); s=socket.create_connection((p.hostname,p.port))
    key='dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ=='
    s.sendall((f'GET {p.path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {p.hostname}:{p.port}\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n').encode())
    response=b''
    while b'\r\n\r\n' not in response: response+=s.recv(4096)
    seq=0
    def send(method,params={}):
        global seq
        seq+=1; ident=seq
        data=json.dumps({'id':ident,'method':method,'params':params}).encode()
        mask=os.urandom(4); n=len(data)
        head=bytes([0x81,0x80|n]) if n<126 else bytes([0x81,0xfe])+struct.pack('!H',n)
        s.sendall(head+mask+bytes(b^mask[i%4] for i,b in enumerate(data)))
        while True:
            h=s.recv(2)
            if not h: raise RuntimeError('Websocket closed')
            n=h[1]&127
            if n==126:n=struct.unpack('!H',s.recv(2))[0]
            elif n==127:n=struct.unpack('!Q',s.recv(8))[0]
            payload=b''
            while len(payload)<n: payload+=s.recv(n-len(payload))
            msg=json.loads(payload)
            if msg.get('id')==ident:return msg
    send('Page.enable');send('Runtime.enable')
    results=[]
    for width,height in [(320,740),(390,844),(768,1024),(1280,900)]:
        send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride',{'width':width,'height':height,'deviceScaleFactor':1,'mobile':width<600})
        send('Page.navigate',{'url':'file:///tmp/opencode/imposter-test.html'})
        for _ in range(100):
            time.sleep(.05)
            val=send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':'document.readyState','returnByValue':True})
            if val.get('result',{}).get('result',{}).get('value')=='complete':break
        time.sleep(.1)
        val=send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':'document.querySelector("#audit-output")?.textContent || "AUDIT NOT FINISHED"','returnByValue':True})
        results.append((width,val.get('result',{}).get('result',{}).get('value')))
    print(json.dumps(results))
finally:
    proc.terminate();proc.wait(timeout=5)

## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game UI while preserving its cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence intact.

## Requirements
- Repair layouts and styling across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Use consistent responsive spacing, typography, cards, buttons, inputs, and interactive states.
- Preserve game flow and avoid unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat the work as UI restoration and polishing, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve `state.phase`, role and word selection, and verbal clue behavior.
- Restore the original stylesheet, then append focused responsive and accessibility refinements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Restored the original stylesheet rules lost from `styles.css`; added responsive layouts, verbal-flow styling, focus-visible outlines, disabled-button states, and reduced-motion handling.
- Chromium browser audit exercised setup, role reveal, typed clues, voting, results, and party/player stats at 320, 390, 768, and 1280px; found no horizontal overflow or elements extending beyond the viewport.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` pass.

### Active
- Finish visual and interaction verification, especially verbal-discussion flow and any remaining clipping concerns.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the tested gameplay screens visually at mobile, tablet, and desktop sizes.
2. Verify the verbal-discussion path and any remaining gameplay interactions.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Restored base styling plus responsive and interaction refinements.
- `app.js`: Existing screen templates, game flow, statistics, and persistence; preserve behavior.
- `index.html`: App shell and stylesheet/font loading.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Mobile screenshot is at `/tmp/opencode/imposter-mobile.png`.
- Browser audit used a temporary test page at `/tmp/opencode/imposter-test.html`; it is not part of the project.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game UI while preserving its cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence intact.

## Requirements
- Repair responsive layouts and styling across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Preserve game flow and avoid unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat the work as UI restoration and polishing, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve `state.phase`, role and word selection, and verbal clue behavior.
- Restore the original stylesheet, then append focused responsive and accessibility refinements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Restored stylesheet rules and added responsive layouts, verbal-flow styling, focus-visible outlines, disabled-button states, and reduced-motion handling.
- Chromium audit exercised setup, role reveal, typed clues, voting, results, and stats at 320, 390, 768, and 1280px; no horizontal overflow or viewport clipping was found.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` pass.

### Active
- Finish visual and interaction verification, especially verbal-discussion flow and remaining clipping concerns.
- Inspect tested gameplay screens visually at mobile, tablet, and desktop sizes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect tested gameplay screens visually at mobile, tablet, and desktop sizes.
2. Identify and exercise the verbal-discussion path; check for clipping and overlap.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Restored base styling plus responsive and interaction refinements.
- `app.js`: Existing screen templates, game flow, statistics, and persistence; preserve behavior.
- `index.html`: App shell and stylesheet/font loading.
- `/tmp/opencode/imposter-mobile.png`: Mobile screenshot from the prior audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/imposter-test.html`: Temporary browser test page.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-audit.py`: Chromium CDP audit script.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The most recent browser audit did not reach verbal discussion; it remained in `clues` at “discussion start”.

import base64, json, os, socket, struct, subprocess, time, urllib.request
PORT=9238
proc=subprocess.Popen(['chromium','--headless=new','--no-sandbox','--disable-gpu','--remote-debugging-port='+str(PORT),'--user-data-dir=/tmp/opencode/cdp-game-profile','about:blank'],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
try:
    for _ in range(100):
        try:
            pages=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/json/list'))
            page=next(x for x in pages if x['type']=='page')
            break
        except Exception: time.sleep(.1)
    u=page['webSocketDebuggerUrl'].replace('localhost','127.0.0.1')
    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    p=urlparse(u); s=socket.create_connection((p.hostname,p.port))
    key='dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ=='
    s.sendall((f'GET {p.path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {p.hostname}:{p.port}\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n').encode())
    response=b''
    while b'\r\n\r\n' not in response: response+=s.recv(4096)
    seq=0
    def send(method,params={}):
        global seq
        seq+=1; ident=seq
        data=json.dumps({'id':ident,'method':method,'params':params}).encode()
        mask=os.urandom(4); n=len(data)
        head=bytes([0x81,0x80|n]) if n<126 else bytes([0x81,0xfe])+struct.pack('!H',n)
        s.sendall(head+mask+bytes(b^mask[i%4] for i,b in enumerate(data)))
        while True:
            h=s.recv(2)
            if not h: raise RuntimeError('Websocket closed')
            n=h[1]&127
            if n==126:n=struct.unpack('!H',s.recv(2))[0]
            elif n==127:n=struct.unpack('!Q',s.recv(8))[0]
            payload=b''
            while len(payload)<n: payload+=s.recv(n-len(payload))
            msg=json.loads(payload)
            if msg.get('id')==ident:return msg
    send('Page.enable');send('Runtime.enable')
    results=[]
    for width,height in [(320,740),(390,844),(768,1024),(1280,900)]:
        send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride',{'width':width,'height':height,'deviceScaleFactor':1,'mobile':width<600})
        send('Page.navigate',{'url':'file:///tmp/opencode/imposter-test.html'})
        for _ in range(100):
            time.sleep(.05)
            val=send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':'document.readyState','returnByValue':True})
            if val.get('result',{}).get('result',{}).get('value')=='complete':break
        time.sleep(.2)
        val=send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':'document.querySelector("#audit-output")?.textContent || "AUDIT NOT FINISHED"','returnByValue':True})
        results.append((width,'vote',val.get('result',{}).get('result',{}).get('value')))
        shot=send('Page.captureScreenshot',{'format':'png','captureBeyondViewport':False})
        open(f'/tmp/opencode/imposter-vote-{width}.png','wb').write(base64.b64decode(shot['result']['data']))
        flow="while(state.phase==='vote'){const voter=state.roles[state.voteIndex];const target=state.roles.findIndex(p=>p.name!==voter.name);document.querySelector('[data-vote=\"'+target+'\"]').click();document.querySelector('#castVote').click()}record('results');document.querySelector('#audit-output').textContent=JSON.stringify(audit);"
        send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':flow,'returnByValue':True})
        time.sleep(.1)
        val=send('Runtime.evaluate',{'expression':'document.querySelector("#audit-output").textContent','returnByValue':True})
        results.append((width,'result',val.get('result',{}).get('result',{}).get('value')))
        shot=send('Page.captureScreenshot',{'format':'png','captureBeyondViewport':False})
        open(f'/tmp/opencode/imposter-result-{width}.png','wb').write(base64.b64decode(shot['result']['data']))
    print(json.dumps(results))
finally:
    proc.terminate();proc.wait(timeout=5)

## Objective
- Restore and polish the existing IMPOSTER game UI while preserving its cream, lime-green, and forest-green design.
- Keep gameplay, settings, scoring, statistics, and persistence intact.

## Requirements
- Repair responsive layouts and styling across mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Preserve game flow and avoid unrelated logic changes.
- Verify gameplay, responsiveness, scrolling, and absence of overlap or clipping.

## Decisions
- Treat the work as UI restoration and polishing, not a game rebuild.
- Preserve `state.phase`, role and word selection, and verbal clue behavior.
- Restore the original stylesheet, then append focused responsive and accessibility refinements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Restored stylesheet rules and added responsive layouts, verbal-flow styling, focus-visible outlines, disabled-button states, and reduced-motion handling.
- Chromium audit reached verbal discussion at 320, 390, 768, and 1280px; no horizontal overflow or viewport clipping was reported.
- Visually inspected verbal-discussion screenshots at 320, 390, and 1280px.
- `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js` passed in the prior audit.

### Active
- Finish visual and interaction verification, including tablet and later gameplay screens such as voting and results.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the 768px verbal-discussion screenshot and remaining gameplay screens at representative sizes.
2. Check scrolling and confirm no overlap or clipping through the later game flow.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `styles.css`: Restored base styling plus responsive and interaction refinements.
- `app.js`: Existing screen templates, game flow, statistics, and persistence.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-audit.py`: Temporary Chromium CDP audit script.
